panels.description: Which node currently holds the highest and the lowest read latency at ${percentile}, named. topk and bottomk are used rather than max and min because they keep the host_name label; max by (cluster) aggregates the node away and leaves the legend naming a cluster instead. Two caveats, both properties of the data rather than faults. These percentiles arrive pre-aggregated from Cassandra's EstimatedHistogram and snap to bucket boundaries, so nodes often hold identical values; where they tie, the choice between them is arbitrary, and if every node ties the same node can legitimately appear as both fastest and slowest. The selected node also changes between scrapes, so a line may switch host across a time range — that is a real change in which node is slowest, not a rendering artefact. The per-node breakdown directly below shows every node at once.
panels.title: Read Latency ${percentile} — slowest and fastest node (${latency_unit:text})

panels.description: Active threads per pool, stacked cluster-wide. Total height = total active threads. Useful for seeing which pools are saturated and what's driving load.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, keyspace, table) (cassandra_table_sstable_count_live{keyspace!~"system.*|sidecar_internal", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"})

panels.description: Compaction backlog against compaction throughput. The pending series is the queue depth; the completed/s series is how fast the node drains it. A rising backlog with a flat completion rate means compaction cannot keep up.
panels.title: Compaction Backlog vs Completion Rate
Hinted Handoff — in progress + accrual rate

targets.expr: max by (cluster) (1 - sum by (cluster, host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])))
min by (cluster) (1 - sum by (cluster, host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])))
avg by (cluster) (1 - sum by (cluster, host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Application Throughput (% time NOT doing GC)

targets.expr: sum by (host_name, jvm_gc_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))

sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_count{job="cassandra", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, host_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_bucket{job="cassandra", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Garbage Collection Time + Pause Percentiles
panels.description: GC time per second, mean pause and p99 pause per node. jvm_gc_name values ending in Cycles are excluded: generational ZGC reports concurrent cycle time under that name, and counting it as pause time makes the ZGC node look worse than the G1 nodes when the opposite is true.

panels.title: JVM Heap Memory
panels.description: Heap use per node. The pool limit series takes the maximum of jvm_memory_limit_bytes across the heap pools, never the sum: generational ZGC reports the whole-heap limit on both the young and the old pool, so summing would double db2 alone. This is the closest OTel equivalent of the old jvm_memory_bytes_max, but not the same concept.

Live bytes as a share of total bytes on disk, per table. A ratio below 1 means obsolete SSTables are still on disk and have not been reclaimed, usually snapshots or compaction inputs that are still referenced.

targets.expr: sum by (keyspace, table) (cassandra_table_disk_space_live_bytes{keyspace!~"system.*|sidecar_internal", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"}) / sum by (keyspace, table) (cassandra_table_disk_space_total_bytes{keyspace!~"system.*|sidecar_internal", cluster=~"$cluster", host_name=~"$host"})

panels.title: Live / Total Disk Space Ratio per Table

panels.description: Least-squares slope of storage load over a 30 minute window, per node. A positive value means the node is accumulating data. This cluster emits no free-space metric (the hostmetrics filesystem scraper is off), so a projected time-to-full cannot be drawn here.
panels.title: Storage Growth Rate per Node

list.description: Derived from a Cassandra-only metric, so it lists database nodes only and can never offer control0 or app0. host_name is carried by every exporter, so the same filter also works on the system and eBPF panels.
list.label: Host

list.description: Which pre-aggregated percentile to read. Cassandra emits these as gauges from its own EstimatedHistogram, so there is no bucket to re-aggregate and no cluster-wide percentile to compute.

list.description: Display scale for the latency panels. The metric is emitted in microseconds and this value is the multiplier applied in the query. Those panels use the short unit and name the scale in the title, so nothing is converted twice.
